chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, from al-Zuhri, who said:

I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both): Which of the acts is best? He said: The arriving and departing [thing]. I said: And what is the arriving and departing [thing]? He said: Opening the Qur'an and closing it; whenever one arrives at its beginning, one departs from its end. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is given the Qur'an by Allah and sees that someone else was given something better than what he was given, then he has belittled a great thing and magnified a small thing.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the arriving and departing' act in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), who defines the 'arriving and departing' (*al-hal al-murtahl*) as the continuous cycle of reciting the Qur'an from beginning to end, symbolizing the believer's spiritual journey. This practice is elevated to the status of the best deed, emphasizing that the Qur'an is the supreme divine gift, and failing to recognize its preeminence over all other blessings constitutes a distortion of spiritual values.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Qasem bin Muhammed al-Esbahani, from Sulayman bin Dawud al-Manqari, from Sufyan bin ‘Uyayna, from Zuhri, that he said:

I said to Ali bin Hussain, peace be upon them both: Which of acts is better? He said: The arriving and departing thing. I said: And what is the arriving and departing thing? He said: To open the Qur’an and seal it; whenever one arrives at its first, one departs at its end. Moreover, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The one to whom Allah gives the Qur’an, and who then sees that someone was given something better than what he was given, then certainly, he has belittled a great thing and magnified a small thing.
